source.effective: 1 July 2021 (Sukuk issuances for financial periods beginning on/after this date)

display_card.one_liner: Governance framework for the entire Sukuk lifecycle — issuance, continuity, restructuring, and maturity.
display_card.what_it_is: Sets out 7 governance organs, 11 governance principles, and detailed Shari'ah-supervisory (SSSB), disclosure, audit and Fatwa requirements covering a Sukuk from pre-issuance through termination/liquidation.
display_card.why_it_matters_to_timeline: First AAOIFI standard to govern Sukuk holistically (vs. SS17's product-level fiqh rules), responding to post-2008 market credibility concerns over asset-transfer authenticity and SSSB independence.

applicability.text: Applies to the originator (IFI, corporate, or government) of a Sukuk or economically similar instrument regardless of nomenclature, for the full lifecycle. In a Sukuk program with multiple tranches, each tranche must independently satisfy the standard.

core_machinery.text: 7 governance organs (TCWG, management, SSSB, trustee, internal audit, external auditor, external Shari'ah auditor — para 10). 11 governance principles mapped to 5 institutional pillars: Shari'ah compliance, accountability, fairness, transparency, responsibility (para 8-9). Lifecycle parts: Pre-issuance (C), Continuity (D), Pre-maturity changes (E), Maturity/liquidation (F), Transparency/disclosure (G).

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: SSSB must be appointed for every Sukuk issuance (existing SSB may double as SSSB with regulatory approval)
SSSB has unrestricted right to all information/records/documents from originator, trustee, advisors
Provisional Fatwa (initial structure) then Final Fatwa (after final documentation review) — final Fatwa must review final rating certificates and legal docs
Fatwa document is mandatory, must be part of legal documentation, and made public via prospectus
Sukuk assets must be transferred to SPV absolutely — legal impediment against originator/creditor claims, no originator control/equity stake in SPV
No recourse to originator for SPV losses unless a Shari'ah-compliant credit-enhancement arrangement is SSSB-approved
External Shari'ah audit at least annually
SSSB periodic report at least annually, addressed to those charged with governance
Change of SSSB member requires approval of trustee, Sukuk-holders/reps, and regulator
Termination must not cause unjustifiable material loss to Sukuk-holders; SSSB approves modus operandi
Restructuring cannot be initiated merely because the original structure has Shari'ah issues, unless the Fatwa-change process (paras 64-66) is followed first

implications: Sukuk product cards in-app should surface the Fatwa lifecycle (provisional → final) and flag structures lacking a genuine/absolute asset transfer to the SPV.
Mandatory annual external Shari'ah audit + SSSB report gives two independent recurring assurance checkpoints usable as compliance-LLM triggers.
5-level Shari'ah-principles hierarchy (para 7(l)) is now confirmed across 6 governance standards (GS1, GS9, GS10, GS11, GS22, GS12) — strong candidate for a standalone cross-cutting timeline node.
limitations: Must be read alongside Shari'ah Standard 17 'Investment Sukuk' (footnote 1) for product-level fiqh rules — SS17 is currently SS-blocked (unreadable scan) in this project.
Transitional provisions mean pre-2021 Sukuk may legitimately not comply with completed lifecycle phases (para 103).

disputes.issue: Increased cost of issuance vs. conventional bonds due to added Shari'ah/audit expert involvement
disputes.resolution: Board accepted added cost as inherent to Sukuk's distinct nature; recommended standardized structures to mitigate cost.

disputes.issue: Standardization of Sukuk structures might hinder innovation
disputes.resolution: Board held standardization enables rather than restricts innovation (e.g. hybrid structures).

disputes.issue: Two-stage Fatwa (provisional + final) seen by some stakeholders as cumbersome/time-consuming
disputes.resolution: Board kept both stages, arguing provisional Fatwa saves time overall and reduces late-stage rejection risk.
'Originator' adopted as the all-encompassing, non-debt-implying term.

disputes.issue: Whether Shari'ah advisory firms (not just individual scholars) can serve as SSSB
disputes.resolution: Permitted if firm has ≥3 Shari'ah board members meeting the standard's requirements.

disputes.issue: Request to mandate disclosure of SSSB remuneration
disputes.resolution: Rejected — treated like legal/rating-agency fees, not required to be disclosed.

disputes.issue: Mandatory transfer of assets to SPV seen as conflicting with market's asset-based (vs asset-backed) practice, and as disguised privatization for sovereign Sukuk
disputes.resolution: Board upheld the true-transfer requirement to protect Shari'ah substance over prevailing market practice.

disputes.issue: Single vs. separate Fatwa for a Sukuk program (multiple tranches)
disputes.resolution: Left to the discretion of the relevant SSB/SSSB.

disputes.issue: Depth of SSSB's documentation review before issuing Fatwa
disputes.resolution: SSSB must confirm in the Fatwa whether full detailed review was performed by each member, and by whom if not.

disputes.issue: Whether internal Shari'ah audit should be mandatory for frequent non-IFI Sukuk originators (governments/corporates lacking such a function)
disputes.resolution: Recommended, not mandated; outsourcing or using general internal audit dept considered acceptable but not preferred.

timeline_bridge.concept_thread: 5-level Shari'ah-authority hierarchy — GS12 para 7(l) restates the identical hierarchy already documented in GS1/GS9/GS10/GS11/GS22.
